summary: Counsel for the Respondent(s) : Subhash Chandran K.R Krishna L.R for Res. 1 M. T. George for Res. 3 1. The Appellant has, in this appeal, assailed the order dated 6[th] September, 2019 passed by 3[rd] Respondent – Kerala State Electricity Regulatory Commission (hereinafter referred to as “the Commission”) in petition bearing No. OA 8 of 2018 filed by the Appellant. Even though, the Appellant had filed the petition under Section 86(i)(e) of the Electricity Act, 2003 for determination of generic tariff for its small hydro 2. Therefore, the crucial issue which arises for our determination in this appeal would be :- 3. Before proceeding to decide the said issue, we find it pertinent to advert to the facts and circumstances of the case in which the petition came to be filed before the Commission by the Appellant. wherein the terms and conditions upon which the project was to be implemented by the Appellant, were stated. 8. It appears that on account of disagreement between the Appellant and 1[st] Respondent with regards to certain terms of the draft PPA, the PPA has remained to be executed between the parties despite the fact 9. It is in this backdrop that the Appellant had approached the Commission by way of petition bearing No. OA 8 of 2018 under section 86(1)(e) of the Electricity Act seeking determination of generic tariff for its small hydro project. The prayer made in the petition is relevant and is extracted herein below:- _“3. The Commission admitted the petition as OA 8/2018. The Commission in view of the decision of the State_ 12. We have heard Learned Counsel for the Appellant as well as Learned Counsels appearing for 1[st] Respondent and 3[rd] Respondent. We have also perused the impugned order as well as written submissions filed by the Learned Counsels. 18. In the instant case, manifestly, the Appellant in its petition before the Commission, had prayed for determination of generic tariff for its 8 MW hydro power project. It is nowhere the case of any of Respondents including the Commission that the Appellant had submitted an application under Regulation 22 for determination of project specific tariff for its small hydro power project. Therefore, the Commission ought to have proceed to determine the generic tariff for the power project of the Appellant. 1[st] July, 2017 issued by the State Government. Copy of such decision/direction dated 1[st] July, 2017 issued by the State Government has not been produced on record by any of the respondents. However, the Appellant has along with the additional documents submitted by way of IA No. 578 of 2025 filed copy of the minutes of meeting dated 1[st] July, 2017 held by Chief Minister of the State of Kerala. Clause 10 of these minutes is relevant and is extracted herein below:- _Electricity Act 2003). A two-judge bench of this Court, speaking through Justice Swatanter Kumar, observed:_ _17. That the state regulatory commissions are not ‘bound’ by the_ _**directions** of the state government, or the Central Government is also evident from the text of Section 108. The provision reads: “In the discharge of its functions, the State Commission shall be guided by such directions in matters of policy .”. This indicates that the state commission shall only be ‘guided’ by the directions issued by the state government and is not automatically bound by them. This interpretation is strengthened by the divergence in the language used in other provisions of the Act, such as Section 11 of the Act which reads as follows:_ _and maintain any generating station in accordance with the directions of that Government” in extraordinary circumstances. This can be distinguished from the language in Section 108, which merely requires that the state commission “be guided by” the directions of the State Government. The provision, in no manner, seeks to control the exercise of quasi-judicial power by the state commissions based on directions issued by the state government.”_ 27. On behalf of the Commission, it was vehemently argued by its counsel as under :- - _(iv) In view of the above, the Commission has decided to determine the project specific tariff in the Appellant’s project. Therefore, soon after admitting the petition, this Commission vide letter dated 04.06.2018 has informed the appellant that, the Commission had decided to determine the project specific tariff of the project, and directed the appellant to submit the additional details for the determination of project specific tariff of the project.”_ 28. We do not find any merit in these submissions on behalf of the Commission. The impugned order of the Commission nowhere reflects that the Commission had proceeded to adopt the parameters notified by CERC for the purpose of determination of tariff for the electricity generated from RE project of the Appellant, in view of Regulation 17(4) of 2015 RE Regulations. We have already extracted the relevant portion of paragraph No. 3 of the impugned order herein above which clearly indicates that the Commission proceeded to determine the project specific tariff for the Appellant’s power project in view of the decision dated 1[st] July, 2017 of the State Government. 29. Thus, in view of the foregoing discussion, the impugned order of the Commission cannot be sustained as the same is absolutely erroneous and flawed. Accordingly, we allow the appeal and set aside the impugned order. The case is remanded back to the Commission with the direction to determine the generic tariff for the power project of the Appellant in terms of the provisions contained in Kerala Small Hydro Power Policy and 2012 RE Regulations. We also direct that in the meanwhile, the Appellant shall be paid interim tariff @Rs.4.65 per unit as used to be paid to it prior to passing of impugned order by the Commission. 30. Needless to say that the Commission shall conclude the exercise within three months from the date of receipt of this judgement. Pronounced in the open court on this 5[th] day of January, 2026.
title: Minar Renewable Energy Projects Private Limited VERSUS Kerala State Electricity Board Limited & Ors
